Class Piece

java.lang.Object
chess.pieces.Piece
Direct Known Subclasses:
Bishop, King, Knight, Pawn, Queen, Rook
public abstract class Piece extends Object
Abstract base class for all six chess piece types.

Holds the state every piece shares (color, current position, whether it has moved) and the movement helpers several subclasses reuse. Each subclass supplies its own movement pattern by overriding isValidPattern(Position, Board); callers work only with Piece references and let polymorphism pick the right rule.

canMoveTo(Position, Board) and possibleMoves(Board) are template methods: the superclass fixes the sequence of checks and subclasses fill in the piece-specific step.

Simplified prototype: moves are not checked for king safety, so a move that leaves one's own king attacked is still accepted.

  • Method Details

    • isValidPattern

      public abstract boolean isValidPattern(Position target, Board board)
      Checks whether moving from this piece's current square to target fits this piece type's movement pattern.

      Implementations check only the shape of the move (and, for pawns, whether the target is empty or holds an enemy). They do not need to check for blocking pieces or friendly destinations; canMoveTo(Position, Board) handles those.

      Parameters:
      target - destination square, never equal to the current position
      board - the board, for pieces whose pattern depends on occupancy
      Returns:
      true if the move matches this piece's pattern
